gold: Mature cystic teratoma in the posterior fossa
e7_s4_rationale: The presence of a cystic mass with a mural nodule in the posterior fossa, as shown on MRI, along with the cyst fluid analysis and the patient's symptoms, is most consistent with Hemangioblastoma. The high-density mass shadow on CT and the mixed signals on MRI also support this diagnosis.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Pilocytic astrocytoma
e7_s4_rejected.why: While pilocytic astrocytoma can present with a cystic component, the location and imaging characteristics are less typical for this diagnosis

e7_s4_rejected.label: Ependymoma
e7_s4_rejected.why: Ependymomas are more commonly associated with the ventricular system and spinal cord, and the imaging findings do not strongly support this diagnosis

e7_s4_rejected.label: Medulloblastoma
e7_s4_rejected.why: Medulloblastoma typically presents in the midline of the cerebellum and has a more aggressive appearance on imaging, which does not match the described case

e7_s4_rejected.label: Meningioma
e7_s4_rejected.why: Meningiomas are usually dural-based and have a different appearance on imaging, with more homogeneous enhancement and a distinct dural tail, which is not described in this case

B07_pred: Hemangioblastoma; Dysplastic Gangliocytoma of the Cerebellum (Lhermitte-Duclos Disease)
